steps.title: Deepen Berakhot: cited teachings and disagreement
steps.reason: Return to Berakhot with the tools to follow a baraita, objection, and distinction.

steps.title: Enter Shabbat: cases, domains, and categories
steps.reason: Use your reading tools in a new legal world built from concrete cases.

steps.title: Enter Eruvin: boundary and measure
steps.reason: Read a tractate where physical space and legal categories meet.

steps.title: Enter Pesachim: action, time, and source
steps.reason: Carry argument mapping into ritual time and practice.

steps.title: Enter Sukkah: validity, measurement, and dispute
steps.reason: Practice reading how a physical condition becomes a legal question.

steps.title: Enter Yoma: preparation, limit, and proof text
steps.reason: Trace a procedure through its stated risk, its limiting principle, and the Gemara's source-based grounding.

steps.title: Enter Bava Metzia: claims and evidence
steps.reason: Bring Gemara tools into civil disputes, competing claims, and evidence.

steps.title: Enter Bava Kamma: categories of damage
steps.reason: Sort a legal field into categories, differentiate them, then find what they share.

steps.title: Enter Ketubot: schedule and institutional reason
steps.reason: Trace a fixed detail to its real reason, then weigh it against a second value the same reason has to balance.

steps.title: Enter Chullin: a rule read through its exception
steps.reason: Follow a broad rule, its narrowing exception, and the condition that reopens it.

steps.title: Enter Niddah: a three-way dispute, held carefully
steps.reason: Track three distinct positions in a live machloket without flattening any of them.

steps.title: Enter Sanhedrin: category, wording, and purpose
steps.reason: Read a Mishnah’s category and examples closely enough to follow the Gemara’s question about why the wording specifies both.

steps.title: Enter Moed Katan: rule and bounded exception
steps.reason: Read a permitted exception through the default restraint, threatened loss, and source limit that keep the exception from swallowing the rule.

steps.title: Enter Nedarim: legal speech and function
steps.reason: Ask what an utterance does in context, then trace competing accounts of its legal force.

steps.title: Enter Nazir: transfer legal speech into status
steps.reason: Carry the Nedarim reading move into a new status while preserving what changes in the new tractate.

steps.title: Enter Rosh Hashanah: calendar, testimony, and authority
steps.reason: Trace how observed time becomes a communal legal decision, then test the limits of testimony.

steps.title: Enter Megillah: public reading and local practice
steps.reason: Read how a shared public obligation can preserve a common text while making room for place and circumstance.

steps.title: Enter Taanit: timing, rain, and communal response
steps.reason: Follow a calendar-based escalation from ordinary practice to communal response without losing the source's thresholds.

steps.title: Enter Chagigah: obligation and exception
steps.reason: Use a pilgrimage obligation to practice reading who is included, who is exempt, and why the category matters.

steps.title: Enter Beitzah: category and reason
steps.reason: Compare a day-one category with its day-two boundary and ask what kind of reason can sustain the distinction.

steps.title: Enter Bava Batra: shared space and evidence
steps.reason: Move from competing claims to the structures that make shared property legible and governable.

steps.title: Enter Makkot: testimony and consequence
steps.reason: Trace how witness status, warning, and consequence interact without collapsing procedural safeguards into outcomes.

steps.title: Enter Shevuot: counted liability and intention
steps.reason: Carry counted-pattern reading into oaths, separating what was said, known, and legally owed.

steps.title: Enter Zevachim: validity and obligation
steps.reason: Read how a mismatched intention can change fulfillment without erasing every legal result.

steps.title: Enter Menachot: parallel, exception, and transfer
steps.reason: Transfer Zevachim's structure into meal-offerings, then let Menachot's exceptions correct the analogy.

steps.title: Enter Bekhorot: status, ownership, and redemption
steps.reason: Follow how firstborn status attaches, changes hands, and reaches a redemption condition.

steps.title: Enter Arakhin: fixed measures and valuation
steps.reason: Read a Torah-defined valuation system by separating fixed categories from the conditions that alter their application.

steps.title: Enter Temurah: substitution and consequence
steps.reason: Test what changes when a consecrated designation is redirected, and what the original act still determines.

steps.title: Enter Keritot: inadvertence and atonement
steps.reason: Distinguish counted liability, knowledge, and atonement when an act was done without full awareness.

steps.title: Enter Meilah: misuse and restitution
steps.reason: Track how benefit from consecrated property produces responsibility, restitution, and a boundary between error and intent.

steps.title: Enter Tamid: ordered daily service
steps.reason: Read sequence, role, and repetition as sources of meaning in a daily service order.

steps.title: Enter Avodah Zarah: commerce and context
steps.reason: Study a time-bounded commercial restriction by separating action categories, reasons, exceptions, and historical setting.

steps.title: Enter Horayot: authority and repair
steps.reason: Follow how an erroneous communal ruling distributes reliance, responsibility, and the work of correction.

steps.title: Enter Yevamot: obligation and exemption
steps.reason: Map family-law categories, levirate obligation, and the exemptions that keep a general rule from becoming careless.

steps.title: Enter Sotah: testimony and uncertainty
steps.reason: Read testimony, procedure, and uncertainty together while preserving the limits of inference.

steps.title: Enter Gittin: document and agency
steps.reason: Trace how intent, representation, delivery, and document validity interact in a legal act.

steps.title: Enter Kiddushin: status and consent
steps.reason: Read acquisition, agency, conditional language, and status as distinct moves in a legal relationship.
